chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Zurara who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The time for Maghrib is when the disc (of the sun) disappears. So if you see it after that, and you have already prayed, then repeat the salat, and your fast continues, and refrain from the food if you had taken something from it.'

key_terms.أَعِدِ الصَّلَاةَ: Repeat the prayer — a legal obligation when the prayer was performed before its valid time
key_terms.الْقُرْص: The disc — refers to the visible circular body of the sun; when it fully disappears below the horizon, Maghrib time begins
key_terms.مَضَى صَوْمُكَ: Your fast continues — meaning the fast remains valid and is not broken by this error
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْمَغْرِبِ: The time of Maghrib — the onset of the sunset prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the time for Maghrib prayer according to Imam al-Baqir, and what should one do if they prayed before sunset?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the precise jurisprudential ruling for the onset of Maghrib prayer time: it begins when the solar disc fully sets below the horizon. The hadith then addresses a practical edge case — if someone prays Maghrib believing the sun has set, but then sees the sun again (meaning they prayed too early), they must repeat their prayer. However, their fast for that day remains valid, and they should stop eating immediately if they had already eaten after the premature prayer. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential precision in determining prayer times and the principle that fasting is not invalidated by an honest mistake.
